title: Baby crib sent flying, 800,000 flee: Typhoon Noul hits China; scary visuals emerge
summary: Typhoon Noul struck parts of China, forcing roughly 800,000 people to evacuate and leaving at least 10 dead. Dramatic footage and images circulated online showing extreme winds overturning objects, including a baby crib sent flying. Authorities have launched emergency responses, issued weather warnings and mobilized shelters and rescue teams.
content:
Typhoon Noul battered parts of China, prompting large-scale evacuations and widespread disruption. Local officials reported that about 800,000 people were moved from vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas as the storm made landfall. Authorities activated emergency response plans and set up temporary shelters to house displaced residents.

The storm was blamed for at least 10 deaths, according to initial reports from local authorities and media outlets. Rescue teams were deployed to assist those affected, and emergency services worked through dangerous conditions to reach cut-off communities. Power outages, flooded streets and damaged infrastructure were reported in several areas.

Disturbing visuals circulated online in the aftermath of the typhoon, with videos and photos showing the force of the winds. One widely shared clip appeared to capture a baby crib being tossed by the gusts, underscoring the sudden and hazardous nature of the storm. Such imagery highlighted concerns about the safety of homes and the vulnerability of residents during extreme weather.

Transportation was disrupted as rail and road services were suspended in impacted zones, and authorities urged people to avoid nonessential travel. Coastal areas were placed under heightened alerts and residents were advised to follow evacuation orders and stay informed through official channels.

Meteorological agencies issued warnings about heavy rain, strong winds and the risk of flash flooding. Officials called for continued caution as cleanup and damage assessments proceeded. Emergency responders focused on restoring essential services, clearing debris and prioritizing the safety of those in temporary accommodation.

As relief efforts continue, local and national authorities signaled the need for ongoing monitoring of affected communities and support for recovery. Investigations and damage tallies were expected in the coming days as officials work to provide aid and repairs to impacted towns and cities.
